title: New to AI gamedev. I want to make a pixelated city (isometric view). Need help for which steps to take here.
author: rvl_16
selftext:
Hey guys, I just got started with Unity, Claude and Blender. Got it all hooked up and managed to work some things out. 

For my game I want the worldmap to be like a isometric pixelated city. Something like this: [https://www.dreamstime.com/pixel-cityscape-digital-nighttime-scene-vibrant-image-showcases-pixelated-night-illuminated-dazzling-array-neon-image366391734](https://www.dreamstime.com/pixel-cityscape-digital-nighttime-scene-vibrant-image-showcases-pixelated-night-illuminated-dazzling-array-neon-image366391734) 

So I want buildings with neon signs on it because it will be a commercial/shopping district.   
I tried some stuff to make some buildings but so far the results are not what I am looking for. Perhaps the prompts are bad. I first started with: "Can you make this building in Unity (and/or Blender)". But that didnt give me satisfying results.   
  
So I asked "What steps do I need to take to make this?". I dont want to buy asset packs since I want to try it myself first with help of Claude. So Claude refers to Unity to build the city code and overall city layout. It further refers to Asesprite to make the neon signs. And Blender to make the buildings. 

As for the buildings, street objects, etc. 

1. Do I need to make doors, windows, street lights, neon signs individually and then assemble it into a building in Blender? 
2. Or what are best steps to take here? 
3. Suggestions for applications (that are free to use) and can hep me in the proces?

I wonder if the image I posted as an example is maybe to complex to build?   
Please note that I want to take time and effort to make it look good. 

Anyway, I appreciate it if some of you more experienced people can help me! Much thanks in advance! And bless all who try to make games here for gamers to enjoy. Even with AI, I noticed its very hard work and takes tons of effort. So bless you all!

comments.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
comments.body:
I'm making my own game with AI too. From my experience, it's better to break things down into smaller pieces instead of asking AI to make an entire building at once. Make the basic building first, then windows, doors, signs and other stuff separately. You can reuse those assets later, so you won't have to make everything from scratch. I'd also start with just one street to see how everything looks together before making a whole city. I'm using Godot myself, so I can't really help much with Unity, but I use Blender for 3D models. For pixel art, you could try LibreSprite. It's free. And be prepared to correct AI. A LOT. Sometimes it does exactly what you want, other times it somehow manages to completely misunderstand the simplest instructions.

And no, I don't think your reference is too complicated. It's just a lot of individual work. AI definitely makes things easier, but you still have to do quite a bit yourself.

replies.author: rvl_16
replies.body:
Thank you for replying. I will look into LibreSprite. I havent heard from that one yet so I will check it out. 

And yes, it seems like making the small pieces is the way to go.

comments.author: AdAggravating435
comments.body: I would build each piece modular to a size and spec. So when you put them together it would fit. You can also use your agent to code things like a randomizer. So like each piece has a designated category.

replies.author: rvl_16
replies.body: Thanks, an agent sounds like a good idea. Means it will work on itself and randomize stuff? Can I limit it so it wont go on forever?

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body:
fwiw that reference is basically 2d pixel art, not 3d, so going blender first might be making it way harder. unity has isometric tilemaps built in, you could do the buildings as sprites in libresprite and snap them on a grid. if you do want blender the usual trick is low poly models + an orthographic camera at an iso angle, render small, then clean up the pixels by hand  
and on the randomizer q thats just a script not an agent. it runs once over a grid size you set so it cant go forever. give it a seed so you can get back a layout you liked
